questions.title: Which film will win the Special Jury Prize at the 2026 Venice Film Festival?
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The Venice Film Festival’s official announcement of its 2026 award winners. Resolution : Resolve to the film awarded the Special Jury Prize at the 2026 festival, once the winner is publicly announced. Accepted Answer Format : The winning film’s title.
questions.current_reasoning: Breaking Aug 24 announcement: Venice Film Festival organizers added 'NAZA' as a late 21st title in the main Golden Lion competition—the sole documentary in the lineup. Directed by Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor (co-directors of Oscar-winning 'No Other Land') and produced/executive-produced by James Wilson and Jonathan Glazer (the exact team behind 'The Zone of Interest' and last year's Venice Grand Jury Prize runner-up 'The Voice of Hind Rajab'), 'NAZA' premieres late in the festival on Sept 10 before a jury chaired by Maggie Gyllenhaal that also includes 'Hind Rajab' director Kaouther Ben Hania, Johnnie To, and Daniel Blumberg. Because documentaries are rarely awarded Best Director, Screenplay, or Acting prizes, strong jury support concentrates directly on Golden Lion, Grand Jury Prize, and especially the Special Jury Prize (matching Venice's track record for urgent political works like 'Green Border'), vaulting 'NAZA' to #1 at 0.09 (replacing 'The Echo Chamber' in top 5). With the competition expanded to 21 films (uniform baseline 0.048) and no premieres until Sept 2, we trim Lee Chang-dong's 'Possible Love' (0.08 -> 0.07) and Werner Herzog's 'Bucking Fastard' (0.07 -> 0.06) while holding Hirokazu Kore-eda's 'Look Back' (0.07) and May el-Toukhy's 'Woman Unknown' (0.07), leaving 64% across the remaining 16 titles until screenings and reviews begin.

questions.title: What immigration status will the Trump administration seek to require for noncitizens to be included in the 2030 US census?
questions.background: The decennial US census affects representation in the House of Representatives and the allocation of federal funding. Trump has previously advocated changing which immigrants are counted.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official Department of Commerce proposal, or reliable contemporaneous reporting explicitly describing its eligibility rules for the 2030 census. Resolution Conditions : Resolve upon the administration's next formal proposal specifying eligibility for the 2030 census, provided it is published by September 30, 2026. Identify the immigration status the proposal requires noncitizens to hold to be included. Publication is sufficient; implementation or judicial approval is not required. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the required immigration status, in one to three words.
questions.current_reasoning: Major update based on leaked Department of Commerce/Census Bureau 2030 proposed residence criteria rule submitted to OMB on June 25 and obtained by Wired (Aug 8) and Talking Points Memo (Aug 11, analyzed by CityLand Aug 17 and The Nation Aug 19). The circulated draft explicitly states that only lawful permanent residents (alongside narrow humanitarian carveouts for approved asylees and approved refugees) would be counted among noncitizens, excluding undocumented immigrants as well as temporary visa holders (foreign students, H-1B workers, TPS, DACA). This strongly elevates 'Lawful permanent resident' (0.35 -> 0.65) and slashes broader categories like 'Lawful status' (0.13) and 'Lawful presence' (0.08), while remaining capped at 0.65 because the text is still an OMB review draft that could be revised or delayed prior to formal Federal Register publication.

questions.title: Who will receive the longest prison sentence at the trial over the July 2023 burglary of Gianluigi Donnarumma's Paris home?
questions.background: Goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma and his partner were attacked during a burglary at their Paris home in July 2023.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The Paris Criminal Court's judgment, as documented by the court or reliable contemporaneous reporting. Resolution Conditions : Identify the defendant receiving the longest total prison sentence in the trial verdict delivered by September 30, 2026. Compare sentences actually imposed, including any suspended portions, rather than sentences requested by prosecutors. Later appeals do not affect resolution. Accepted Answer Format : The defendant's name as publicly reported.
questions.current_reasoning: July 11, 2026 AFP/Le Parisien/L'Equipe reporting officially confirmed the Paris Criminal Court (tribunal correctionnel) trial of the three adult defendants for September 10-11, 2026, eliminating postponement risk past Sept 30. The two minor suspects were already tried separately in juvenile court in early July (receiving 4 and 3 years, including 1 year suspended), so they are definitively excluded. The July 11 indictment details further strengthen Ilyas Kherbouch's ('Ganito', 21) position as clear favorite for the longest sentence: beyond his principal-mastermind designation, 7-year prior for the Simone Zanoni home-jacking, and March 2026 Villepinte prison escape, investigators attributed direct SMS instructions on the eve and night of the burglary to his line and found photos of the bloodied, sequestered third adult defendant on Kherbouch's phone. Co-mastermind Khyan M. ('Kiki', 21) remains reported solely with an initialed surname (0.10, with 0.12 left for Khyan M.'s full surname if published at trial, a tie, or the third defendant).
